the neuropsychology in MS is associated with the underlying pathology, and that the neuropsychological deficits are associated with brain structure and function, particularly in the frontal lobe.

the cognitive, affective, and behavioral aspects of MS and the underlying brain changes.
the cognitive, emotional, and behavioral aspects of multiple sclerosis (MS) in relation to brain structure and function, and how these aspects relate to everyday life.

the cognitive deficits in MS are heterogeneous in their presentation, with some cognitive deficits being more prevalent than others, and with the deficits varying in severity across individuals.
the cognitive and emotional changes associated with MS are not due to any single factor, but instead are the result of multiple factors, such as demyelination, axonal loss, and inflammation.

the neuropsychology and neuroimaging of MS have progressed substantially in recent years, but that there remain many unanswered questions and challenges for future work.
